findings.desc: core/proofstory.ts:1326-1367 buildScopeShrinkageDecision: withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs are derived only from the current call args (optionalStringArray(args.x)), never merged with existing.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs. If scope_shrinkage_decision_set is invoked twice under the same decisionId (e.g. withdraw CHK-002 in call 1, then withdraw AB-1 in call 2 without repeating withdrawnChecklistItemRefs), the persisted decision.json silently narrows to only the latest calls refs, so scope_shrinkage_decision_get under-reports the cumulative withdrawal history for that decisionId. The actual checklist item status / proofstory.json bindingDispositions remain correct (stamped durably at write time, not re-derived from this field), and the empty-scope floor still works correctly because it unions the fresh decision with the already-persisted contract.bindingDispositions -- so this is an audit-trail/read-model completeness gap in decision.json, not a gating bypass. Worth a merge-with-existing fix or an explicit doc note that repeat calls under one decisionId must re-supply the full ref set.

concept-incompleteness: packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts buildScopeShrinkageDecision (~line 1323) rebuilds withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs/evidenceRefs from args ONLY (optionalStringArray(args.X, ...)), never merged with existing.X. Reproduced: seed a story, call scope_shrinkage_decision_set withdrawing CHK-002 (decision.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs=[CHK-002], decisionId=SD-x) then call it again withdrawing AB-1 only (same decisionId, reused since args.decisionId omitted) -> decision.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs becomes [] even though checklist.json still correctly shows CHK-002 status=withdrawn decisionRef=SD-x. The decision record (the promised single authorizing record both layers cite, CHK-003) becomes a false/incomplete audit trail of what it actually authorized after a second legitimate call under the same decisionId -- contradicting the storys own storage-honesty principle. Compounding: withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom (core/proofstory.ts) is imported into handlers/proofstory.ts but never called there, so unlike bindings (withdrawnBindingIdsFrom feeds effectiveAcceptanceBindings), there is no symmetric checklist-side consumer of the decisions own arrays -- only the per-item stamp on checklist.json keeps things functionally correct, so the decision.json array drift is currently latent (no gate breaks) but is a real half-migrated inconsistency in the new vocabulary the story introduced. No smoke test exercises calling scope_shrinkage_decision_set twice under the same decisionId with different ref sets.

handlers/proofstory.ts:75-88 normalizeScopeRefArray duplicates core/proofstory.ts:258-267 optionalStringArray (same non-empty-string-array-with-dedup logic, comment even says it mirrors the core helper) instead of exporting and reusing it. Low-severity DRY nit: if the core validation rule ever changes, the handler copy can silently drift out of sync since nothing enforces they stay identical.
